newsitem.title: UK: How a country applies to join the ERM.
newsitem.headline: How a country applies to join the ERM.

text.p: Italian Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said Italy expected to return the lira to Europe's exchange rate mechanism by the end of November, with 1,000-1,050 per mark seen as the best rate.
(* Lira in ERM end-Nov at 1,000/1,050/mark-minister)
Here is a brief summary of the procedure for joining or rejoining the ERM, which currently groups 10 of the European Union's 15 currencies.
* Britain was the last country to be allowed to declare its entry rate unilaterally when it took sterling into the ERM in 1990. It was forced out along with the lira two years later.
Any country joining or rejoining the ERM now will have to negotiate the rate at which its currency should join the system.
* Once a country has decided it wants to join the ERM, it asks for a meeting of the EU's monetary committee, a secretive grouping of senior finance ministry and central bank officials.
The committee, which might meet in Brussels during a weekend when markets are closed, would decide whether and at what central rate the currency could join.

* Decisions can be taken very quickly, since the EU is routinely monitoring the economies of all its member states. A monetary committee can be convened in a matter of hours, following informal telephone contacts between capitals.
* However, if the committee fails to reach an agreement, there may be a ministerial meeting the following day.

* There is no formal voting procedure for admitting new ERM members. "It is done as an inter-governmental agreement," a Commission official said recently in Brussels. "Typically there is a consensus found."

The official added, "In taking a decision on those things the monetary committee...would also be looking at the convergence situation, in particular to be clear that the rate chosen would be consistent with the degree of convergence."
* Once in, an ERM member country must keep its currency inside the agreed fluctuation bands -- and preferably as close as possible to its central rate.
* In response to currency turbulence in 1992 and early 1993, the ERM's fluctuation bands were widened in August 1993 to 15 percent either sider of central rates from 2.25 or six percent.

* An ERM member state must be prepared to take the lead in supporting its currency, through direct intervention or changed economic policies. It must accept a pre-emptive devaluation or revaluation if the central rate becomes untenable.
* Britain and Italy have been floating outside the currency grid since September 1992, Greece has never been a member and Sweden is contemplating membership.
* There is some debate about whether membership of the ERM is a prerequisite for joining the EU's planned single currency.

Countries including France and Germany argue that ERM membership is a condition for joining the single currency. Sweden and Britain argue that a stable currency, not formal ERM participation, is the key.
This debate is set to rage until EU leaders meet in early 1998 to decide which countries qualify.
The EU's monetary committee agreed in October to bring the Finnish markka, which had floated for four years, into the grid at a central rate of 3.04 to the mark.
The move threw the spotlight onto Italy. The decision also heightened the debate over possible participation in neighbouring Sweden.
